Desferrioxamine has been associated with fetal ab- normalities in animals, and is generally only recommended in pregnancy if the benefits are considered to outweigh the risks. A review1 of pregnancy outcome following iron overdose found that of 66 patients reported to the UK Teratology Information Service, 35 of whom had received desferrioxamine, 7 gave birth to infants with malformations (severe in one).
